newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Computerised trade makes splash at Karachi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Computerised trade makes splash at Karachi bourse.

text.p: Computerised trading has made its first big impact on share prices at the Karachi Stock Exchange, analysts said on Thursday.
A sharp rise in Hub Power Company Ltd (Hubco) and other bellwether stocks in after-hours computerised trading on Wednesday pushed the 100-share index up 6.82 points to 1,769.43.
The index had ended at 1,758.08 points, a fall of 4.53 points, at the close of normal trading.

"The CTS (computerised trading system) was very helpful in updating Hubco after its GDR (global depositary receipt) rate was revised upwards abroad on Wednesday," dealer Ali Raza of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities said.

Hubco rose 1.35 rupees to 42.75 on a turnover of 391,500 shares after dealers learned that its GDR had risen to $25.75/26.50 from 25.00/25.75, Raza said. Hubco had closed at 41.40 at the end of official trading at 2.35 p.m. (0935 GMT).

The CTS, which operates from 3.30 p.m. to 5.30 p.m. (1030 to 1230 GMT), was introduced in December 1995. At least 288 of 783 listed companies can be traded on the system, but dealing has so far been limited to a few scrips.
Interest in Hubco surged on Wednesday after a board meeting to discuss its results for the six months ended December 31.
The Karachi Stock Exchange plans further moves towards computerisation, but is awaiting equipment from abroad. It has set no date for a full switch to a screen-based system.
The closing rates of CTS trade are taken as the opening rates for floor trading in the next trading hall session.
Transactions are electronically transmitted to the exchange's clearing house for settlement. No verification is required and they are settled under a normal clearing schedule.
